parsed.explanation: No statute criminalises trans identity or same-sex intimacy, but the 2025 UN submission documents current law-enforcement abuse targeting transgender people — harassment at identity checks and arbitrary arrests on vague public-order grounds — plus 2020 reports of violent detentions. There is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination ground, and no domestic recourse for an outed visitor, while societal stigma is pervasive and official posture is disengagement. Counterweights: functioning asylum protection machinery (trans refugee granted status 2022, gender-identity-aware SOPs) and no documented trans-specific killings or entry-screening rules. Patterned police targeting with thin recourse sits between the 0.45 and 0.55 anchors, closer to 0.45.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented at entry; no airport or border-screening evidence. No LGR path exists, so document-marker mismatch persists, but no rule or practice of secondary screening for it is recorded.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch becomes an exposure only upon later police identity checks, which are documented sites of trans-targeted harassment.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arbitrary arrests of transgender people on vagrancy/public-order grounds (2025 UN submission) and violent detentions reported in 2020 — severity tier 3 with a violent-custody element.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for police custody; asylum/migration SOPs are protective but only within protection procedures.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A routine identity check can escalate into arrest and violent detention with no anti-discrimination remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented — no facility, bathroom or custody-placement rules specific to trans people appear.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Patients' Rights Policy (2018) guarantees equal health-service access regardless of gender, applying to public and private sectors.

care_services.exposure: Not documented — no refusals of care, medication seizure, or HRT access findings recorded.
care_services.protection: 2018 health policy grants equal entitlement to services regardless of gender; operates nationwide across sectors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police actively target and harass transgender people at identity checks; blackmail and arrests of LGBT people documented (2016); presidential non-engagement and church condemnation signal official indifference.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None for street-level enforcement; a minister publicly backed a gay singer (2019), a minor positive signal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Vagrancy/morality provisions serve as the enforcement lever against gender-nonconforming people though identity itself is not criminalised.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented — no youth-specific findings on schools, bullying, medication or care access.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Violent police detentions of trans people (2020 report); neighbour harassment of LGBT people documented; social stigma pervasive; no trans-specific killing data and no background denominator.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented — no hate-crime statute or working police recourse for trans victims; LGBTIQ groups cannot register openly (2024 NGO law).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims cannot rely on police, who are themselves documented perpetrators.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No domestic non-discrimination claim (constitutional grounds omit gender identity); no path to align documents; LGBTIQ association barred from open registration.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Asylum SOPs (2014/2024) explicitly protect by gender identity; a trans claimant received refugee status (2022); 2024 immigration/asylum protections for LGBTQ people documented as operating.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protection machinery works inside asylum channels only; an ordinary visitor has no equivalent remedy for police abuse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Drellia's registry creates universal bureaucratic exposure with little recourse; here the exposure is targeted police abuse at identity checks and arbitrary arrest — similar tier-2/3 severity, slightly worse state hand, slightly narrower breadth, landing at the same target level.

Ostrovia has sporadic harassment with some complaint channels; here police abuse is patterned (UN submission, 2020 violent detentions) and remedies for street-level victims are essentially absent, so this jurisdiction sits below 0.55.

Karthovia features systematic stop-and-interrogate instructions with defiant courts; here abuse is documented but with dated specific incidents, no evidence of systematic passport confiscation or file-keeping, and functioning asylum protections — materially above 0.35.
Vellmaris has national equality law and working complaint mechanisms; here constitutional protections omit gender identity, no remedy exists, and police are the perpetrators — clearly below 0.65.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of non-criminalisation without protection: identity itself carries no penalty, but police use vagrancy and public-order provisions as a documented lever against transgender people at identity checks, with 2020 violent detentions, no anti-discrimination recourse, no legal gender recognition, and societal stigma reinforced by official disengagement. An outed visitor faces harassment, arbitrary arrest and possible violent detention — tier-2/3 exposure — but not organised sweeps, imprisonment campaigns or lethal state policy. The asylum/migration protection machinery (gender-identity-aware SOPs, a 2022 grant) shows the state can protect trans people within formal channels, and no border, facility, care or minor-specific restriction is documented. Open questions — entry screening practice, post-2020 violence frequency — hold the score at the 0.45 level rather than below.
